common.appDescription: The student platform for coursework, schedules and collaboration.

home.title: One academic platform over the systems you already run
home.subtitle: StudViro reads your student information system and gives students, teachers and administrators a single dashboard, calendar and course page — without replacing anything.

problem.title: Two systems, two logins, two answers
problem.body: A timetable lives in one system and a deadline in another. A grade exists as a calculation, a proposal and an official record, and nothing shows a student which one they are looking at. Every question that spans both systems becomes the student's job to assemble.

one.title: Nothing is migrated
one.body: One record, entered once, read everywhere it matters.

two.title: Nothing is guessed
two.body: Every value on screen names the system it came from and when.

three.title: Nothing is over-shared
three.body: What a person sees is decided by a scoped permission, on the server.

features.title: What it does today
features.subtitle: Shipped and in use, not roadmap.

dashboard.title: A dashboard that answers "what now?"
dashboard.body: This term's courses, the latest results and the rest of this week on one screen, each item linking through to the detail behind it.

calendar.title: One week, both layers
calendar.body: Classes and exam terms in a single week view, filterable by course and by type, for courses you attend and courses you teach.

course.title: A course page with everything on it
course.body: Staff, your own enrolment, study groups and results in one place, instead of four tabs across two systems.

exams.title: Exam terms you can act on
exams.body: Seats, registration window and examiner, filterable by whether you may register — and when you may not, the server says why.

sync.title: One record, many views
sync.body: Freshness per domain, per-run results, retries and a history, plus an on-demand report of every record where the source and the platform disagree.

audiences.title: Built for the three people who use it
audiences.subtitle: The same record, read three ways.

students.title: Students
students.body: One timetable, one place to see where a grade came from, and an exam registration that tells you why a seat is out of reach.

teachers.title: Teachers
teachers.body: The offerings you lead, who is enrolled in each, and your own teaching week — without opening a second system to assemble it.

institutions.title: Institutions
institutions.body: Run the whole academic year in one place: the catalogue, enrolment, timetables, exams and grades, with every permission checked at the scope it belongs to.

connect.title: 1. Set up the institution
connect.body: An administrator creates the institution, its org units and its first administrator, then enters the programmes and courses it offers.

import.title: 2. Fill the year
import.body: Terms, offerings, timetables and exam terms go in once, into 25 canonical tables. Every row is institution-scoped and soft-deleted rather than erased.

use.title: 3. Use one surface
use.body: Students, teachers and registrars each get a dashboard, a calendar and a course page over the same record, showing only what their role permits.

trust.title: What we do with your data
trust.subtitle: The parts a registrar asks about first.

credentials.title: Credentials are write-only
credentials.body: Passwords are argon2. Sessions rotate. Nothing sensitive is echoed back, not even to an administrator.

permissions.title: Permissions carry a scope
permissions.body: Every grant names both what it permits and where. Holding the permission to read enrolments never opens a list of someone's classmates.

provenance.title: Every record says where it came from
provenance.body: Every row is institution-scoped, soft-deleted rather than erased, and carries who changed it and when, so a disputed value can be traced.

readOnly.title: Read-only, for now
readOnly.body: Reads are scoped by permission at the scope that grants it. A student reading their own grade and a registrar reading the roster travel different paths on purpose.

replace.question: Does this replace AIS2 and Moodle?
replace.answer: That is the point. StudViro is the system of record: the institution enters its own data and there is no upstream. The registry half is built; the learning half — assignments, submissions and marking — is next.

lms.question: Which systems can you connect today?
lms.answer: The registry: programmes, courses, offerings, enrolment, timetables, exams and grades. Course materials, assignments and submissions are the next phase.

accounts.question: How do people get accounts?
accounts.answer: An institution onboards with us. Accounts are invited rather than opened from the public internet, and university single sign-on is on the roadmap.

conflict.question: What happens when two systems disagree?
conflict.answer: The platform reports it. A reconciliation check names every record that is missing, stale or in conflict, per domain, on demand.

cost.question: What does it cost?
cost.answer: We do not publish a price. Terms depend on your size and which systems you run, so a conversation is the honest answer.

closing.title: See it against your own systems
closing.body: Bring one department and one term. We will show you what the platform covers today and what it does not yet.

footer.tagline: One academic platform over the systems a university already runs.

meta.title: For students
meta.description: One timetable, grades that say where they came from, and exam registration that explains itself.

hero.title: Stop assembling your own timetable
hero.subtitle: Your courses, your week and your results in one place — read from your university's systems, not retyped into another one.

week.title: Your whole week in one view
week.body: Classes and exam terms as two layers of the same week, filterable by course and by type.

courses.title: Your courses, by term
courses.body: Every enrolment with its status, and a course page with the staff, your study groups and your results on it.

grades.title: A grade that explains itself
grades.body: Calculated, proposed and official are shown as what they are, each with the system it came from and when it was last seen.

exams.title: Registration that gives you a reason
exams.body: Register and cancel from any exam term. When you cannot, the server answers why instead of greying out a button.

notifications.title: Told once, not five times
notifications.body: When an exam term is published, moved or cancelled you hear about it — deduplicated to one message per term per day.

roadmap.title: Not yet
roadmap.body: Assignment hand-in and course materials are next. Browsing the catalogue and enrolling yourself already works.

closing.title: Ask your university about it
closing.body: StudViro is deployed by an institution, not signed up for individually. If your university is evaluating it, this is the page to send them.

meta.title: For teachers
meta.description: The offerings you lead, who is in them, and your teaching week — in one place.

hero.title: Your teaching, without the second login
hero.subtitle: The offerings you lead, the students in each of them and your own week, over the same record your students read.

offerings.title: Everything you lead, by term
offerings.body: Your teaching assignments with your role on each and how many students are actually enrolled.

roster.title: A roster that agrees with itself
roster.body: The student list and the enrolment count exclude withdrawn and rejected enrolments, and always match.

calendar.title: One week, teaching included
calendar.body: The calendar scopes to the offerings you teach as well as the ones you attend.

course.title: The same course page your students see
course.body: Staff, study groups and exam terms, so a question about a course has one answer rather than two.

roadmap.title: Not yet
roadmap.body: Entering or proposing a grade, managing an offering and editing its timetable are permissions the platform grants and no screen yet uses. Grading stays in your existing system until that lands.

closing.title: See it with your own courses
closing.body: A demo runs against a populated institution, so you can look at an offering you recognise.

meta.title: For institutions
meta.description: One academic platform an institution runs itself: catalogue, enrolment, timetables, exams and grades in one record.

hero.title: One surface over the systems you already run
hero.subtitle: One system of record, not a layer over two others. The institution enters its own data, and every audience reads the same record through the permissions it holds.

connectors.title: Roles that mean something
connectors.body: Eight canonical roles over a scope tree. A student role derives from an active programme membership and a teacher role from a teaching assignment, so neither is handed out by mistake.

sync.title: Every change, on the record
sync.body: Freshness per domain, per-run results, per-record failures, retries and a full run history.

reconciliation.title: Disagreements, named
reconciliation.body: An on-demand report of every record that is missing, stale or in conflict between the source and the platform, per domain.

roles.title: Scoped role administration
roles.body: Grant and revoke permissions against a scope, with the hierarchy enforced on the server rather than hinted at in the interface.

model.title: A canonical model with provenance
model.body: 25 institution-scoped tables covering the whole academic year, with soft deletion and keyset pagination throughout.

containers.title: Containers you host
containers.body: A NestJS API on PostgreSQL and Redis, with migrations gated on startup so a replica never serves a schema it is behind.

contract.title: A generated API contract
contract.body: The client is generated from a drift-checked OpenAPI document, so the interface and the API cannot disagree.

mock.title: Evaluate without access
mock.body: A deterministic generator seeds a realistic synthetic university of around five thousand linked records, so a pilot can start with something to look at.

roadmap.title: On the roadmap, honestly
roadmap.subtitle: Designed, not shipped. Ask about timelines rather than assuming them.

lms.title: Learning-system integration
lms.body: Course materials, assignments, submissions and marking, natively.

writeback.title: Bulk entry and migration
writeback.body: Today the platform reads. An exam registration made here does not yet reach your system of record.

sso.title: University single sign-on
sso.body: OIDC against your identity provider, blocked on institutional client registration.

export.title: Data export and audit
export.body: Personal-data export and a readable audit trail are planned and not yet built.

closing.title: Bring one department and one term
closing.body: The most useful demo runs against a scope you recognise. Tell us how your year is shaped and we will show you what the platform covers.
